data.note:
Reflection: unblinded as methotrexate, DHFR inhibitor annotated as DNA replication.

Mechanism: antifolate antimetabolite blocking reduced folates for thymidylate/purine synthesis, arresting S-phase - reviewed as antimetabolites PMID:22049385, methotrexate/pralatrexate PMID:26433846, antifolate resistance PMID:17333344, megaloblastic change from folate blockade PMID:6450011. DNA-replication stress phenocopies DNA damage in nuclear morphology.

What I saw: strong low nuc_dna_mean z -10 to -12, large spread cells area z +5 to +7, low density, 0 mitotics, intact filamentous tubulin and cortical actin. I used this to rule out mitotic/cytoskeletal classes correctly but split DNA damage vs DNA replication.

Atlas failure: NSC 2/2 tie DNA damage vs Protein degradation with very low cosine 0.31-0.40 = weak evidence; k-list had DNA damage 4/10 and DNA replication 3/10 with reference DNA-damage and replication compounds interleaved. I broke tie toward DNA damage on summed similarity, over-weighting weak signal. Replicate variability at 1uM (nuc_dna_mean z -11.7 vs -2.06) and flat nuc_dna_mean dose-response rho -0.21 should have lowered confidence in DNA-damage call.

Lesson: with low similarities and DNA-damage/replication neighbours mixed, default should stay near DNA replication for antimetabolite-like enlarged low-DNA interphase phenotype; follow-up gamma-H2AX/53BP1 + DNA-content flow with a reference compound of each class would discriminate.

reflection.text:
The run correctly placed the phenotype on the DNA axis. All quantified wells showed extreme low nuc_dna_mean z around -10 to -12 with enlarged cell_area z +3 to +7 and low density, and intact tubulin/actin on describe_phenotype rightly excluded microtubule, actin and mitotic classes. Keeping DNA replication at 0.28 then 0.25 alongside DNA damage reflected the atlas k-neighbour split.

The error was over-reading a weak NSC comparison as decisive for DNA damage. The final vote was a 2-2 tie with Protein degradation with very low absolute similarities 0.31-0.40, broken only by summed similarity 0.777 vs 0.648 and 4/10 vs 3/10 k-neighbours, which is not discriminative between DNA damage and DNA replication stress that phenocopy as low-DNA enlarged cells. I treated large low-DNA cells as damage rather than antimetabolite S-phase blockade by methotrexate DHFR inhibition PMID 26433846, PMID 22049385.

Acquisition choices locked in the mistake. Sampling only 1, 3 and 10 uM stayed in a saturated regime where dose_response for nuc_dna_mean was flat rho -0.21 p=0.79, while cell_area rho +0.95 only confirmed non-specific enlargement, and the 10 and 3 uM wells actually voted Protein degradation. No low-dose onset wells were acquired to test where DNA loss emerges, and the unknown microscopist call in e5 was not followed up.
what_was_right: Recognized strong DNA-axis signal: nuc_dna_mean z -11.7, -10.1, -12.7 with cell_area z +5.6 to +7.7 across e2, e3, e7.
Correctly excluded cytoskeletal/mitotic classes using low eccentricity, increased major axis without mitotic figures, and intact tubulin/actin in e5.
Kept DNA replication as joint top hypothesis throughout (0.28 in e6, 0.25 in e12) reflecting 4/10 vs 3/10 k-neighbour split in e4/e9.
what_was_wrong: Broke 2-2 NSC tie on summed similarity 0.777 vs 0.648 despite absolute similarities only 0.31-0.40, overstating support for DNA damage at p=0.42.
Misinterpreted enlarged low-DNA, low-density phenotype as DNA damage rather than DHFR-inhibitor replication stress phenocopy that also gives megaloblastic enlargement.
Acquired only high saturated doses 1, 3, 10 uM; dose_response showed flat nuc_dna_mean rho=-0.21 p=0.79, so no discriminating onset was measured and 10 and 3 uM wells voted Protein degradation.

citations.claim: Methotrexate acts as an antifolate dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor that deprives cells of nucleotides for DNA replication.
Antimetabolites block DNA synthesis rather than directly inflicting DNA breaks like classic DNA-damaging agents.
Antifolate drugs cause megaloblastic enlarged-cell morphology with impaired DNA synthesis.
Antifolate resistance mechanisms center on the folate pathway and dihydrofolate reductase.

**Question.** Which mechanism-of-action class explains this compound's phenotype in MCF-7 cells?

14. `lookup_compound` — Protocol step after the review: identify the unblinded specimen in PubChem and ChEMBL.
15. `search_literature` — Retrieve papers on methotrexate DHFR mechanism to explain DNA replication annotation.

## Hypothesis history

- after step 6: DNA damage 0.28, DNA replication 0.28, Protein degradation 0.18, Protein synthesis 0.08, Microtubule destabilizers 0.03, Microtubule stabilizers 0.03, Actin disruptors 0.02, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.02, Cholesterol-lowering 0.02, Eg5 inhibitors 0.02, Epithelial 0.02, Kinase inhibitors 0.02
- after step 12: DNA damage 0.42, DNA replication 0.25, Protein degradation 0.15, Microtubule destabilizers 0.02, Microtubule stabilizers 0.02, Actin disruptors 0.02, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.02, Eg5 inhibitors 0.02, Cholesterol-lowering 0.02, Epithelial 0.02, Kinase inhibitors 0.02, Protein synthesis 0.02

## Conclusion

**DNA damage** (stated probability 0.42); key evidence e2, e3, e7, e9, e5, e11.

Why: NSC vote tied 2-2 but summed similarity and 4/10 neighbours favour DNA damage; intact microtubules/actin rule out mitotic classes.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Stain for DNA-damage response (gamma-H2AX / 53BP1 foci) plus DNA-content flow cytometry and a reference compound of the leading class as positive control to test arrest vs replication stress.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Approve: Evidence weakly but consistently favours DNA damage over runner-ups. NSC vote is tied 2-2 with Protein degradation, but summed similarity (0.777 vs 0.648) and k-neighbours (4/10 DNA damage vs 3/10 DNA replication, 1/10 Protein degradation) favour DNA damage; no well voted DNA replication. Phenotype (enlarged low-DNA cells, low count/mitotics, intact tubulin/actin) excludes cytoskeletal/mitotic classes but is non-specific among DNA classes, so stated 0.42 vs 0.25/0.15 is appropriately modest. Conclusion agrees with protocol_call. Budget is exhausted (0 left), and no free re-analysis would change the NSC vote, so no affordable decisive experiment remains.

## Unblinding

Compound: **methotrexate** (PubChem CID [126941](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/126941))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: Dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **DNA damage**, BBBC021 annotates **DNA replication**.

The final call is the nearest-neighbour vote over the 4 wells the agent chose (2/4). The Scientist's own call was **DNA damage** (agrees; wrong).

## Reflection

The run correctly placed the phenotype on the DNA axis. All quantified wells showed extreme low nuc_dna_mean z around -10 to -12 with enlarged cell_area z +3 to +7 and low density, and intact tubulin/actin on describe_phenotype rightly excluded microtubule, actin and mitotic classes. Keeping DNA replication at 0.28 then 0.25 alongside DNA damage reflected the atlas k-neighbour split.

The error was over-reading a weak NSC comparison as decisive for DNA damage. The final vote was a 2-2 tie with Protein degradation with very low absolute similarities 0.31-0.40, broken only by summed similarity 0.777 vs 0.648 and 4/10 vs 3/10 k-neighbours, which is not discriminative between DNA damage and DNA replication stress that phenocopy as low-DNA enlarged cells. I treated large low-DNA cells as damage rather than antimetabolite S-phase blockade by methotrexate DHFR inhibition PMID 26433846, PMID 22049385.

Acquisition choices locked in the mistake. Sampling only 1, 3 and 10 uM stayed in a saturated regime where dose_response for nuc_dna_mean was flat rho -0.21 p=0.79, while cell_area rho +0.95 only confirmed non-specific enlargement, and the 10 and 3 uM wells actually voted Protein degradation. No low-dose onset wells were acquired to test where DNA loss emerges, and the unknown microscopist call in e5 was not followed up.

What was right:
- Recognized strong DNA-axis signal: nuc_dna_mean z -11.7, -10.1, -12.7 with cell_area z +5.6 to +7.7 across e2, e3, e7.
- Correctly excluded cytoskeletal/mitotic classes using low eccentricity, increased major axis without mitotic figures, and intact tubulin/actin in e5.
- Kept DNA replication as joint top hypothesis throughout (0.28 in e6, 0.25 in e12) reflecting 4/10 vs 3/10 k-neighbour split in e4/e9.

What was wrong or missed:
- Broke 2-2 NSC tie on summed similarity 0.777 vs 0.648 despite absolute similarities only 0.31-0.40, overstating support for DNA damage at p=0.42.
- Misinterpreted enlarged low-DNA, low-density phenotype as DNA damage rather than DHFR-inhibitor replication stress phenocopy that also gives megaloblastic enlargement.
- Acquired only high saturated doses 1, 3, 10 uM; dose_response showed flat nuc_dna_mean rho=-0.21 p=0.79, so no discriminating onset was measured and 10 and 3 uM wells voted Protein degradation.

Proposed next experiment: Test EdU S-phase incorporation and DNA-content cell-cycle profile with and without leucovorin/folinic acid rescue, comparing methotrexate to a reference antimetabolite and a direct DNA breaker as controls to distinguish replication blockade from DNA damage response.

## Citations

Citations verified: 4/4

- PMID [26433846](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26433846/): Methotrexate and Pralatrexate. *Dermatol Clin* (2015) — Methotrexate acts as an antifolate dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor that deprives cells of nucleotides for DNA replication.
- PMID [22049385](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22049385/): [Antimetabolites]. *Bull Cancer* (2011) — Antimetabolites block DNA synthesis rather than directly inflicting DNA breaks like classic DNA-damaging agents.
- PMID [6450011](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/6450011/): Drug-induced megaloblastic change. *Clin Haematol* (1980) — Antifolate drugs cause megaloblastic enlarged-cell morphology with impaired DNA synthesis.
- PMID [17333344](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17333344/): Molecular basis of antifolate resistance. *Cancer Metastasis Rev* (2007) — Antifolate resistance mechanisms center on the folate pathway and dihydrofolate reductase.
